availability.p: This electronic TEI edition was created for educational and scholarly purposes as part of coursework in textual encoding and digital humanities using Oxygen XML Editor.

sourceDesc.p: The source text consists of serialized newspaper installments published in the Seattle Union Record between October and December 1926. The articles discuss police administration, corruption, vice regulation, urban politics, and social conditions in Seattle during the 1920s.

normalization.p: This transcription follows a diplomatic approach. Original spelling, capitalization, punctuation, and formatting have been preserved as closely as possible. No modernization of spelling or grammar has been undertaken.

punctuation.p: Original punctuation, spacing, paragraph divisions, and line breaks were retained whenever visually evident in the source document.

correction.p: Apparent typographical irregularities and spelling inconsistencies were preserved without editorial correction.

interpretation.p: Editorial intervention was kept to a minimum. Structural features such as headings, section titles, and date markers were preserved because they contribute to the organization and rhetorical structure of the text.
